issues.failure_explanation: Parseval applied to D^{r}(f-f_N) via the displayed coefficient identity gives \|D^{r}(f-f_N)\|^2 = sum over k of lambda_r(k)|<f-f_N, H_{k+r}>|^2, and <f-f_N, H_{k+r}> vanishes exactly when |k+r|<=N. Hence the inner sum must run over |k+r|>N, not |k|>N. As printed the identity is false and strictly smaller than the norm: for d=1, alpha=1, f=H_{N+1} one has f_N=0 and \|f-f_N\|^2_{H^1_rho} = 1+(N+1) = N+2, while the printed right-hand side equals 1 (the r=1 contribution requires k=N, which the condition k>N excludes). Because the printed expression is smaller than the true norm, its vanishing does not, as written, imply \|f-f_N\|->0.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the inner summation condition |\mathbf{k}|>N by |\mathbf{k}+\mathbf{r}|>N (equivalently, write the tail as \sum_{|\mathbf{k}|>N} (\prod_j k_j!/(k_j-r_j)!) |\langle f, H_{\mathbf{k}}\rangle|^2). The corrected sum is the tail of the convergent Parseval series of D^{\mathbf{r}}f, hence tends to 0 as N->infinity, completing the proof with no other change.
issues.overall_effect: The displayed justification in the proof of Proposition prop:dense is a false identity, so the density conclusion is not established as written. The statement of prop:dense is nevertheless correct, and once the index is corrected the proof works; the tensor-product construction of Section 2.2 and the sparse-grid analysis of Section 3 that rest on prop:dense are unaffected.
issues.title: Wrong truncation index in the Parseval tail identity of the density proof
issues.why_classification: The proposition's statement is true and the repair is a one-condition correction of a summation index in a single display; no new argument is needed and no claim, rate, or downstream result changes.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: and let $\xi_{1},\dots,\xi_{n}$ be the roots of the univariate Hermite

issues.failure_explanation: The displayed equality, justified by 'since I^uni_{\bar\ell_1} is interpolatory', amounts to \int I^uni_{\bar\ell_1}(p_n)\rho dx = Q^uni_{\bar\ell_1}(p_n). But the two operators sample at different node sets: Q^uni_{\bar\ell_1} is the n_{\bar\ell_1}-point Gauss--Hermite rule at the zeros \xi_1,...,\xi_n of H_{n_{\bar\ell_1}} (n=n_{\bar\ell_1}), where the fooling function p_n vanishes, so Q^uni_{\bar\ell_1}(p_n)=0 (precisely the vanishing used in Theorem thm:GH-lower-bound-general, where S_Lambda(h_Lambda)=0). In contrast, I^uni_{\bar\ell_1} interpolates at the n_{\bar\ell_1}+1 zeros \eta_i of H_{n_{\bar\ell_1}+1}, which strictly interlace the \xi_j, so p_n(\eta_i)>0 at the interior interpolation nodes and \int I^uni_{\bar\ell_1}(p_n)\rho dx = \sum_i \omega_i p_n(\eta_i) > 0 because the interpolatory (Gauss) weights \omega_i are positive. The two sides therefore differ, the equality is false, and the subsequent reduction of the L^1_rho interpolation error to the established univariate integration lower bound (the final display of the proof) is invalid: no lower bound on \|p_n - I^uni_{\bar\ell_1}(p_n)\|_{L^1_rho} is actually obtained.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use the fooling function matched to the interpolation nodes: with m := n_{\bar\ell_1}+1, take h_Lambda(x) = p_m(x_1), where p_m vanishes at the m zeros of H_m. Then I_Lambda(h_Lambda) = I^uni_{\bar\ell_1}(p_m) = 0, so \|h_Lambda - I_Lambda(h_Lambda)\|_{L^1_rho} = \int p_m \rho dx \ge c_\alpha m^{-\alpha/2}\|p_m\|_{H^\alpha_\rho} by the same cited univariate analysis used in Theorem thm:GH-lower-bound-general; the point-count comparisons are unchanged since m = n_{\bar\ell_1}+1 \asymp n_{\bar\ell_1} and, under the growth hypothesis, n_\ell+1 \asymp n_\ell, so the isotropic relation N \asymp_d n_{L-d+1}(\ln n_{L-d+1})^{d-1} still yields both stated bounds. (Equivalently, redefine I^uni_\ell to interpolate at the zeros of H_{n_\ell}; then the printed chain holds verbatim since both Q^uni_{\bar\ell_1}(p_n) and \int I^uni_{\bar\ell_1}(p_n)\rho vanish.)
issues.overall_effect: Both claims of Theorem thm:added-1 -- the lower bound c_{\alpha,d}N^{-\alpha/2} for the L^1_rho error of sparse-grid Gauss--Hermite interpolation over index sets that are downward-closed in one direction, and the isotropic bound with the additional logarithmic factor -- are unproven as written. No other labelled result depends on this theorem.
issues.title: Interpolation lower-bound proof equates quadrature and interpolation errors on different node sets
issues.why_classification: The proof contains a false equality, and repairing it requires replacing the fooling-function construction (or the interpolation node set in the theorem statement) and reworking the display -- more than a local typo correction -- but the repair is contained within this single application theorem, uses only tools already present in the paper, and preserves both stated bounds and their rates; the theorem has no dependents.
